newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities soft as dlr/mark falters.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities soft as dlr/mark falters.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options remained soft, particularly the shorter dates, as the spot dollar moved further away from 1.72-mark resistance and 120-yen support, dealers said.

"A lot of people call you up for quotes in short dates and they just go away when you come up with lower bid/ask," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York. "It seems they were all trying to sell.
Traders said the market appeared to be expecting spot to stay largely range-bound until the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
While many traders saw a 50-50 chance the Federal Reserve could tighten credit at the FOMC meeting, they said it still seemed too early to buy gamma.
A high-gamma position, typically a result of buying short-dated options, has quicker premium acceleration when spot rates swing around but is also vulnerable to time decay.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options stood at 9.1/9.3 percent at U.S. midsession, a touch off overnight highs and little changed from Tuesday.
The back end was also steady, with one-year 9.6/9.7 percent, maintaining a positive slope in the volatility curve.

The dollar failed at a high just above 1.71 marks after a mild overnight rally and ground down below 1.70 marks in U.S. trading. But because the market's risk perception was still to the dollar's upside, the slide triggered only modest bid for volatilities, traders said.
Dollar/mark reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, were still slightly favoring mark puts, with one-month 25-delta pegged at 0.1/0.3 percent.
Growing prospects of near-term range trade were spurring the use of some cheaper exotic options, such as knock-outs, by end-users, dealers said.
"There were a lot of range binaries," said a U.S. bank dealer in New York.

Dollar/yen volatilities were also softer as the dollar hovered in the mid-122 yen area, right in the middle of a perceived 120-125 yen medium-term range. One-month volatility stood at 9.2/9.4 percent against 9.4/9.6 late on Tuesday.

Due to heavy end-user buying of low delta dollar puts in mid to late February, when the dollar's uptrend stalled, bank dealers were collectively short in strikes below 120 yen, hedging some of that risk with long at-the-money positions, dealers said.

Because at-the-moneys have the steepest time decay and because those hedge positions become excessive when volatility levels decline and shrink gamma, vega and other risk parameters of the low-delta strikes, the recent decline in volatilities has become a self-feeding process, Okada noted.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities were firmer but off overnight highs as cable, which had dropped below $1.60 earlier, drifted above lows below $1.59.
One-month cable and one-month sterling/mark volatilities were about a quarter point above their late Tuesday levels at 8.9/9.2 percent and 9.4/9.7 percent respectively.
